'''Erick O'Brien Green II''' (born May 9, 1991) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Pallacanestro Cantù|Cantù]] of Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA). He finished the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13 NCAA Division I season]] as the top scorer in the nation at 25.0 [[point (basketball)|points]] per game. Green was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] with the 46th overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]], but was later traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]].

==High school career==
Green was born in [[Inglewood, California]] but grew up in [[Winchester, Virginia]].<ref name=BIO>{{cite web| title =11 Erick Green| work =HokieSports.com| url =http://www.hokiesports.com/mbasketball/players/green_erick.html| access-date =February 27, 2013| archive-date =June 2, 2016| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20160602202153/http://www.hokiesports.com/mbasketball/players/green_erick.html| url-status =dead}}</ref> He spent the first three years of his prep career at his hometown's [[Millbrook High School (Virginia)|Millbrook High School]], before transferring for his senior year to [[Fairfax, Virginia|Fairfax]]'s [[Paul VI Catholic High School]].<ref name=BIO/> Between the two schools, Green earned four varsity letters.<ref name=BIO/> In his lone year at Paul VI, he led the Panthers to a state championship (coincidentally, Green had led Millbrook to a state championship the previous season) and was named the 2009 Division I Independent League Player of the Year.<ref name=BIO/> After Paul VI's championship he was named an EA Sports All-American.<ref name=BIO/> ''[[The Washington Post]]'' also selected him to their All-Metro Team, the [[Associated Press]] picked him as their Virginia Group AA Player of the Year, and Green was named the district and region player of the year.<ref name=BIO/>

==College career==
[[File:Erick Green.jpg|thumb|right|140px|Green playing for Virginia Tech, 2013]]
Green struggled his [[freshman]] season in [[2009–10 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2009–10]] and averaged just 2.6 points per game and shot 29.3% from the field.<ref name=SR>{{cite web| title =Erick Green Stats| work =Sports-Reference.com| publisher =Sports Reference LLC| url =https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/erick-green-1.html| access-date = March 1, 2013}}</ref><ref name=GYM>{{cite web| last =Giannotto| first =Mark| title =For Virginia Tech's Erick Green, success at the rim started in the gym| work =WashingtonPost.com| date =February 20, 2013| url =https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/for-virginia-techs-erick-green-success-at-the-rim-started-in-the-gym/2013/02/20/fc5eff40-7b7d-11e2-9a75-dab0201670da_story.html| access-date = March 1, 2013}}</ref> His lack of production, he later admitted, "turned [him] into a gym rat" and motivated him to work harder than everyone else to improve his game.<ref name=GYM/> Each progressive season he increased his scoring, rebounding and assist averages.<ref name=SR/> By his senior season in 2012–13, and while leading NCAA Division I in scoring for most of the year, the media was discussing Green as a [[dark horse]] candidate for [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Atlantic Coast Conference Player of the Year]].<ref name=GYM/><ref name=TEEL>{{cite web| last =Teel| first =David| title =Teel Time: Is nation's top scorer, Virginia Tech's Erick Green, the ACC's player of year?| work =DailyPress.com| date =February 5, 2013| url =http://www.dailypress.com/sports/teel-blog/dp-teel-time-green-acc-poy,0,3334715.story| access-date =March 1, 2013| archive-date =July 30, 2014| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20140730013657/http://www.dailypress.com/sports/teel-blog/dp-teel-time-green-acc-poy,0,3334715.story| url-status =dead}}</ref> Despite his production, the Hokies finished the year with a 13–19 overall record, including a 4–14 conference record where they finished in last place. On March 12, 2013, Green was named the ACC Player of the Year by the ACC's media selectors ([[2012–13 Miami Hurricanes men's basketball team|Miami]]'s [[Shane Larkin]] was the coaches' pick).<ref>{{cite web| last =Wood| first =Norm| title =Virginia Tech's Erick Green earns ACC's player of the year honors| work =DailyPress.com| date =March 12, 2013| url =http://www.dailypress.com/sports/colleges/virginia-tech/dp-spt-tech-erick-green-acc-player-of-year-0313-20130312,0,862133.story| access-date =March 12, 2013| archive-date =October 28, 2014| archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20141028201527/http://www.dailypress.com/sports/colleges/virginia-tech/dp-spt-tech-erick-green-acc-player-of-year-0313-20130312,0,862133.story| url-status =dead}}</ref> He joined [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland]]'s [[Len Bias]] (1985–86) as the only two players of the year who competed for teams with losing ACC records.<ref>{{cite web|last=Giannotto| first=Mark |title =Virginia Tech's Erick Green named ACC player of the year| work =WashingtonPost.com| date =March 12, 2013| url =https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/virginia-techs-erick-green-named-acc-player-of-the-year/2013/03/12/09be5fb8-8b38-11e2-9f54-f3fdd70acad2_story.html| access-date = March 16, 2013}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Montepaschi Siena (2013–2014)===
On June 27, 2013, Green was selected by the [[Utah Jazz]] with the 46th overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]]; his rights were immediately traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]]. He joined the Nuggets for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Denver Nuggets announce 2013 Summer League roster|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-announce-2013-summer-league-roster|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2013|access-date=August 26, 2013}}</ref> where he averaged 9.3 points, 2.2 rebounds and 1.8 assists in six games.

On August 26, 2013, Green signed a one-year deal with [[Montepaschi Siena]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A|LBA]].<ref>{{cite web|title=MONTEPASCHI SIENA nabs rookie scorer Green |url=http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2013-14-signings/i/115229/8177/montepaschi-siena-nabs-rookie-scorer-green |work=Euroleague.net |date=August 26, 2013 |access-date=August 26, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130831112125/http://www.euroleague.net/euroleaguenews/transactions/2013-14-signings/i/115229/8177/montepaschi-siena-nabs-rookie-scorer-green |archive-date=August 31, 2013 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Mens Sana Siena announced Rochestie, Green, Hunter and English|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/105423/mens-sana-siena-announced-rochestie-green-hunter-and-english.html|work=Sportando.com|date=August 26, 2013|access-date=August 26, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140724082531/http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/105423/mens-sana-siena-announced-rochestie-green-hunter-and-english.html|archive-date=July 24, 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 45 Italian league games for Siena, in 2013–14, he averaged 10.8 points, 1.5 rebounds, and 1.1 assists per game.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://web.legabasket.it/player/?id=GRE-ERI-91 |title=Erick Green TOTALI STAGIONE . |access-date=2016-10-12 |language=it |archive-date=2016-10-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161013080713/http://web.legabasket.it/player/?id=GRE-ERI-91 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He also averaged 11.1 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 1.0 assists per game, in 10 games played in the [[EuroLeague]] that same season.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/competition/players/showplayer?pcode=005159&seasoncode=E2013 EuroLeague 2013-14 STATISTICS.]</ref>

===Denver Nuggets (2014–2015)===
In July 2014, Green re-joined the Denver Nuggets for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Nuggets prospect Erick Green benefits from overseas experience|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/nuggets-prospect-erick-green-benefits-overseas-experience|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2014|access-date=July 23, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=2014 Summer League Player Profile – Erick Green|url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague/2014/players/sl_erick_green/|work=NBA.com|access-date=July 23, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150410081414/http://www.nba.com/summerleague/2014/players/sl_erick_green/|archive-date=April 10, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On August 1, 2014, he signed a three-year, $2.3 million contract with the Nuggets after averaging an impressive 16.6 points per game over five Summer League contests for the team.<ref>{{cite news|title=Denver Nuggets Sign Erick Green|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-sign-erick-green|access-date=August 1, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=August 1, 2014}}</ref> On January 20, 2015, he was assigned to the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Nuggets Assign Erick Green to Fort Wayne Mad Ants|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-assign-erick-green-fort-wayne-mad-ants|access-date=January 20, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=January 20, 2015}}</ref> Five days later, he was recalled by the Nuggets.<ref>{{cite news|title=Nuggets Recall Green from Fort Wayne|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-recall-green-fort-wayne|access-date=January 25, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=January 25, 2015}}</ref> In the Nuggets' season finale on April 15, he had a season-best game with 17 points, 7 assists, 4 rebounds and 1 steal in a loss to the Golden State Warriors.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/g/greener01/gamelog/2015/|title=Erick Green 2014-15 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref>

In July 2015, Green re-joined the Nuggets for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]] where he averaged 14.8 points, 1.4 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 1.8 steals in five games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.roanoke.com/sports/colleges/va_tech/former-virginia-tech-star-erick-green-excited-for-year-in/article_21e6860c-cba5-5112-b3a3-6f2219cc04b6.html|title=Former Virginia Tech star Erick Green excited for Year 2 in NBA|work=Roanoke.com|date=August 8, 2015|access-date=August 8, 2015}}</ref> On November 5, 2015, he was waived by the Nuggets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-kostas-papanikolaou|title=Nuggets Sign Kostas Papanikolaou|work=NBA.com|date=November 5, 2015|access-date=November 5, 2015}}</ref>

===Reno Bighorns and Utah Jazz (2015–2016)===
On November 21, 2015, Green was acquired by the [[Reno Bighorns]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://reno.dleague.nba.com/news/bighorns-acquire-former-nba-player-erick-green/|title=BIGHORNS ACQUIRE FORMER NBA PLAYER ERICK GREEN|work=NBA.com|date=November 21, 2015|access-date=November 21, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151212050758/http://reno.dleague.nba.com/news/bighorns-acquire-former-nba-player-erick-green/|archive-date=December 12, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his debut for the Bighorns later that night, scoring 23 points in 35 minutes off the bench against the [[Los Angeles D-Fenders]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20151121/rnolad/|title=D-Fenders Hold Off Bighorns At Home|work=NBA.com|date=November 21, 2015|access-date=November 21, 2015|archive-date=November 25, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151125041833/http://dleague.nba.com/games/20151121/RNOLAD/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 29, 2016, he was named in the West All-Star team for the 2016 [[NBA Development League All-Star Game|NBA D-League All-Star Game]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/2016-nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters/|title=Sixteen NBA Veterans Headline Rosters for NBA Development League All-Star Game Presented By Kumho Tire|work=NBA.com|date=January 29, 2016|access-date=January 29, 2016|archive-date=February 7, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170207115139/http://dleague.nba.com/news/2016-nba-development-league-all-star-game-rosters/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On January 26, 2016, Green signed a 10-day contract with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-erick-green-10-day-contract|title=Jazz Sign Erick Green to 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=January 26, 2016|access-date=January 26, 2016}}</ref> The next day, he made his debut for the Jazz in a 102–73 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]], recording four points and one assist in four minutes of action.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160127/CHAUTA/gameinfo.html|title=Hood scores 24 as Jazz defeat Hornets 102-73|work=NBA.com|date=January 27, 2016|access-date=January 28, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160204004743/http://www.nba.com/games/20160127/CHAUTA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=February 4, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On February 5, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Jazz.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-sign-erick-green-second-10-day-contract|title=Jazz Sign Erick Green to a Second 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=February 5, 2016|access-date=February 5, 2016}}</ref> On February 15, the Jazz did not renew his contract, making him a free agent. Four days later, he re-joined the Bighorns.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/green-rejoins-the-bighorns/n-5102326|title=Green Rejoins the Bighorns|work=OurSportsCentral.com|date=February 19, 2016|access-date=February 20, 2016}}</ref> At the season's end, he was named to the [[All-NBA Development League Team|All-NBA D-League First Team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/2015-16-all-nba-dleague-teams-release/|title=NBA Development League Announces 2015-16 All-NBA D-League Teams|work=NBA.com|date=April 29, 2016|access-date=April 30, 2016|archive-date=September 4, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160904054918/http://dleague.nba.com/news/2015-16-all-nba-dleague-teams-release/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Olympiacos (2016–2017)===
On July 15, 2016, Green signed a two-year deal with [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos Piraeus]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/206434/erick-green-signs-with-olympiacos.html|title=Erick Green signs with Olympiacos|work=Sportando.com|date=July 15, 2016|access-date=July 15, 2016}}</ref> On February 2, 2017, Green recorded a season-high 25 points, shooting 10-of-13 from the field, along with three rebounds and two assists in a 90–75 win over [[BC UNICS|UNICS Kazan]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Unics Kazan vs. Olympiacos Piraeus - Game|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=164&seasoncode=E2016|access-date=October 26, 2018|work=EuroLeague.net|date=February 2, 2017}}</ref> Green helped Olympiacos to reach the [[2017 EuroLeague Final Four|2017 EuroLeague Final]], where they eventually lost to [[Fenerbahçe Basketball|Fenerbahçe]].

===Valencia (2017–2018)===
[[File:Erick Green 32 Valencia Basket EuroLeague 20180201 (cropped).jpg|140px|thumb|Green with Valencia in 2018]]
On July 21, 2017, Green signed with Spanish club [[Valencia Basket]] for the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Valencia adds scoring ace Green|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/7ym9optfjm8jjhhg|access-date=July 21, 2017|work=Euroleague.net|date=July 21, 2017}}</ref> Green helped Valencia to win the [[2017 Supercopa de España de Baloncesto|2017 Spanish Supercup]] and was named the Tournament MVP after averaging 15.5 points in two games.

===Fenerbahçe (2018–2019)===
On October 26, 2018, Green signed with the Turkish team [[Fenerbahçe Basketball|Fenerbahçe]] as an injury cover for [[Tyler Ennis (basketball)|Tyler Ennis]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Fenerbahce signs Erick Green|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/fenerbahce-signs-erick-green/|access-date=October 26, 2018|work=Sportando.basketball|date=October 26, 2018}}{{Dead link|date=November 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> On July 10, 2019, Green and Fenerbahçe officially parted ways.

===Fujian Sturgeons (2018–2019)===
In July 2019, Green signed a one-year deal with the [[Fujian Sturgeons]] of the  [[Chinese Basketball Association]] (CBA).<ref>{{cite news |last1=Moody |first1=Walt |title=Green signs to play in China |url=https://www.winchesterstar.com/winchester_star/green-signs-to-play-in-china/article_fd8a9588-a392-5767-b62b-8965ed3a6a3d.html |access-date=January 9, 2020 |work=[[The Winchester Star]] |date=July 19, 2019}}</ref>

===Coosur Real Betis (2020)===
On January 28, 2020, he has signed with [[Real Betis Baloncesto|Coosur Real Betis]] of the [[Liga ACB]]<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/real-betis-makes-erick-greens-signing-official/|title=Real Betis makes Erick Green's signing official|date=January 28, 2020|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=January 29, 2020|last1=Lupo |first1=Nicola }}</ref>

===Bahçeşehir Koleji (2020–2021)===
On June 25, 2020, he has signed with [[Bahçeşehir Koleji S.K.|Bahçeşehir Koleji]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Spain/news/632470/Bahcesehir-tabs-Erick-Green,-ex-Real-Betis|title=Bahcesehir tabs Erick Green, ex Real Betis|date=June 25, 2020|publisher=Eurobasket.com|language=En|access-date=June 25, 2020}}</ref>

===Hapoel Holon (2022)===
On September 28, 2022, he has signed with [[Hapoel Holon B.C.|Hapoel Holon]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/hapoel-holon-lands-erick-green/|title=Hapoel Holon lands Erick Green|last=|first=|date=September 28, 2022|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=September 28, 2022|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref>

===KK Budućnost (2022–2023)===
On December 29, 2022, he signed with [[KK Budućnost|Budućnost VOLI]] in the [[Prva A Liga]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/erick-green-joins-kk-buducnost/|title=Erick Green Joins KK Buducnost|last=|first=|date=December 29, 2022|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=December 29, 2022|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref>

===Napoli Basket (2024–2025)===
On October 23, 2024, he signed with [[Napoli Basket (2016)|Napoli Basket]] of the [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/napoli-basket-officially-signs-erick-green/|title=Napoli Basket officially signs Erick Green|last=|first=|date=October 23, 2024|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=October 23, 2024}}</ref>

=== Pallacanestro Cantù (2025–present) ===
On December 15, 2025, he signed with [[Pallacanestro Cantù|Cantù]] of Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]] (LBA).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pallacanestrocantu.com/cs-erick-green/|title=S. Bernardo Water Strengthens with Erick Green|last=|first=|date=December 15, 2025|website=pallacanestrocantu.com|publisher=|language=it|access-date=January 15, 2026}}</ref>
